title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Ch. 7: Socrates v. Comelec — The Three-Term Limit
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Chapter 7: CJP's account of Socrates v. Comelec and Mendoza v. Comelec, testing the limits of the constitutional three-term limit on elective local officials
sub_topics: The three-term limit (Constitution Art. X; RA 7160) and 'voluntary renunciation' as non-interruption
Socrates v. Comelec — recall election and the three-term bar
Related precedents: Borja, Lonzanida, Adormeo, Frivaldo
signature_phrases: shall serve for more than three consecutive terms

stances.claim: The three-term limit bars a fourth consecutive term, but its application turns on whether service was interrupted (e.g., by recall or renunciation).

notable_anecdotes: Socrates arose from a recall election in Puerto Princesa testing the three-term bar.
one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 7 analyzes Socrates v. Comelec and Mendoza v. Comelec, which tested the constitutional three-term limit on elective local officials (Constitution Art. X; RA 7160). CJP explains how the limit — and the rule that 'voluntary renunciation' does not interrupt consecutive terms — was applied against the backdrop of precedents like Borja, Lonzanida, and Adormeo.
